scientific_question: Can genomic relatedness, floral traits, pollinator visits and fruit production be aligned at the same plants or patches and ordered prospectively to test relational eco-genetic functional fate?

source.title: Data from: Quantitative genetic analysis of floral traits shows current limits but potential evolution in the wild

claim_limits: Pollinator sampling is described as 569 observation surveys and 364 insect visits across six Ulex sites; no same-individual visitation–genotype–fruit join is established by the paper.
Genotypes and genomic relatedness alone do not identify ecological interaction state.
Fruit production assessed in the same reproductive season is not an independent multiyear forward functional-fate endpoint.
Published selection/heritability conclusions are prior art, not fresh EGWE evidence.
No raw source rows, outcomes, or regressions may be inspected or fitted during schema discovery.
no_pseudo_replication: Do not treat pollen census windows or SNP marker columns as independent biological populations.

SNP.genotypes.csv.description: 10421 SNP markers / 225 plants per README; column orientation not yet verified

executed_receipt.readme_interaction_grain: Each row is a separate 3-minute census on Ulex plants; flowers and visits counted within an observation patch. No plant identifier is defined for this file.
executed_receipt.readme_reproductive_grain: Each plant has mean floral traits and twig fruit counts, keyed by ind; floral.traits includes replicate flower IDs.
